results.title: Salman City To Get Central Market, Supermarket And Sports Facilities
results.description: New projects aim to provide residents with shopping, dining and recreation within the growing city Salman City is set to receive a central market, a large supermarket and new sports facilities as part of the second phase of construction and development works on three commercial and service plots. The central market on Plot 11 will cover 1,478.72 square metres and include dedicated sections for meat, fish and vegetables, along with small shops and restaurants. Plot 16 has been allocated for a supermarket with a built-up area of 3,534.66 square metres, while Plot 17 will feature two football pitches and two drive-through restaurants. Together, the three projects account for about 5,230.72 square metres of built-up area and intend to provide essential commercial, social and recreational facilities as Salman City continues to expand.

results.title: Foreign Investment Rises To BD17.64bn
results.description: Finance, manufacturing and professional services lead the portfolio Foreign investment in Bahrain grew by almost half a billion dinars in a year, despite slipping in the first three months of 2026. The stock of foreign direct investment stood at BD17.64 billion at the end of March, up BD449.4 million, or 2.6 pc, from BD17.19bn a year earlier. It was, however, down BD140.8m, or 0.8 pc, from BD17.78bn at the end of December. Finance and insurance dwarfed every other field, accounting for BD11.49bn, or 65.2 pc of the total. Manufacturing came second with BD2.29bn, followed by professional, scientific and technical work at BD1.06bn. Electricity, gas, steam and air-conditioning supply held BD741.86m in foreign investment, while wholesale and retail trade, including vehicle repairs, accounted for BD628.03m. Property stood at BD611.92m, with information and communications at BD493.83m. The figures also covered mining and quarrying, transport and storage, hotels and food services, education, administrative work and support services. Bahrain’s foreign investment stock stayed above BD17bn throughout the past year. results.title: Crescent Spotted Over UAE: What Rabi Al Awwal Means And When The Holiday Falls
results.description: UAE observatory captures Rabi Al Awwal crescent as Prophet Mohammed’s Birthday draws near Abu Dhabi: The International Astronomical Centre has shared images of the crescent moon marking the beginning of Rabi Al Awwal 1448 AH, the Islamic month in which Muslims commemorate the birth of the Prophet Muhammed (PBUH). The crescent was photographed from the centre’s Al Khatim Astronomical Observatory after sunset on Thursday, 13 August. The first image released by the centre shows a single exposure without image stacking, while the second combines a number of images to make the slender crescent more clearly visible. The International Astronomical Centre maintains dedicated observations for each Hijri month, including crescent visibility maps, sighting reports from observers around the world and information on the official start of the month in different countries. The sighting draws attention to Rabi Al Awwal not only as the third month of the Islamic lunar calendar, but also because its 12th day is widely observed as Al Mawlid Al Nabawi, or the birthday of the Prophet Mohammed. results.title: Motorsport Team Prepares For Sepang F1 Race
results.description: A national motorsport team has been sent to Malaysia to map out how Bahrain will help run the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit from October 2 to 4. The Bahrain Motor Federation delegation inspected the track, garages, starting area and other key parts of the circuit as planning for the Formula One weekend moves into a more detailed stage. The team also met Sepang International Circuit staff and representatives of Malaysia’s motorsport federation to work through race control, staffing, scrutineering, transport and safety plans. Part of the visit focused on how many Bahraini marshals and organisers will be needed, where they will be posted and how work will be split across the circuit during the race weekend. Scrutineering staff reviewed checks on the cars and the FIA rules that circuits must meet before staging a Formula One World Championship event. Accommodation, local transport and other needs for the Bahraini contingent were also discussed with Malaysian counterparts and other parties involved in the race. results.title: Unlicensed Building Demolished In East Riffa
results.description: Southern Municipality continues crackdown on building and land-use violations The Southern Municipality has demolished an unlicensed building in Block 919, East Riffa, as part of ongoing efforts to remove violations and enforce municipal regulations. The campaign was carried out under the Municipalities Law No. 35 of 2001, Building Regulation Law No. 13 of 1977 and Public Roads Occupation Law No. 2 of 1996. The municipality said the campaign aims to remove encroachments, improve compliance, preserve the appearance of residential areas and protect public safety. Similar enforcement operations are also under way in the Northern Governorate. In Al Ramli, authorities have removed 47 of 61 illegal structures identified along Shaikh Khalifa bin Salman Street and Shaikh Zayed Street, with further sites targeted in the next phase. According to the Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture, construction without a permit accounts for 68 per cent of building violations.

results.title: U.S. Stocks Move Toward Records As Inflation Eases And Oil Prices Fall
results.description: U.S. stocks moved closer to record highs on Thursday as easing inflation and lower oil prices boosted investor confidence, while falling Treasury yields added further support to equities. The S&P 500 gained 0.5%, putting it on track to challenge the record reached the previous week. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.6%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 123 points, or 0.2%, by late morning. Investor sentiment improved after data showed U.S. wholesale prices increased 4.7% in July from a year earlier, down from 5.5% in June and slightly below economists’ expectations. The figures followed a similar easing in consumer inflation reported a day earlier. The softer inflation readings reduced expectations of another Federal Reserve interest-rate increase in September. Traders were pricing in about a 34% chance of a rate hike, down from roughly 50% two days earlier. Such an increase would be the Fed’s first in more than three years. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.64%, compared with 4.68% on Wednesday. Lower yields can make stocks more attractive while reducing borrowing costs. Oil prices also supported markets, with Brent crude falling 1.1% to $88.03 a barrel amid continued geopolitical uncertainty. results.title: Sharjah Starts Traffic Diversions From Monday Over Etihad Rail Project
results.description: Sharjah Roads and Transport Authority (SRTA) announced partial opening of traffic between University City and the Institutes Land area by providing two traffic lanes in each direction, starting from Industrial Area 17, passing through University Bridge and reaching University City, as part of a road project to access the Etihad Rail Station. The work also includes partial closure and diversion of traffic from Industrial Area 17 towards Mleiha Street with the provision of alternative routes that allow access to services and facilities surrounding the area, according to the routes shown in the approved traffic plan. The traffic diversions will be implemented starting from Monday, August 24, 2026 and will continue until Sunday, October 4, 2026, according to the alternative routes specified in the plan broadcast by SRTA on its social media platforms, thereby ensuring the continuity of traffic and access to all destinations in that area. results.title: Two Children Hear “You’re A Failure” — Only One Believes It
results.description: A child’s sense of self-worth can determine whether hurtful words leave a temporary wound or become a lasting belief. At that moment, certified parenting coach Tuqa Marhoon says many parents focus on the same questions: Who said it? How should they be punished? Should the child change schools? But she says a more important question is often overlooked: What happened inside the child after he heard those words? Children gradually build their understanding of who they are through the messages they repeatedly hear and the relationships and experiences they have each day. A child who regularly hears, “I love you,” “I see you,” and “your place with me does not change even when you make a mistake” can develop a stronger and more stable sense of self-worth. But when a child’s value becomes linked to grades, behaviour, comparisons with others or approval from other people, hurtful comments can have a much deeper impact. Marhoon illustrates the difference with a simple thought experiment: Two children hear the same sentence—“You are a failure.” The first child is hurt but tells himself: “He is wrong.
